title: TAROT: A CXL SmartNIC-Based Defense Against Multi-bit Errors by Row-Hammer Attacks
problem: Row Hammer attacks cause multi-bit uncorrectable errors (UEs) in DRAM that exceed ECC correction capabilities and crash systems. These UEs occur at specific DRAM addresses determined by manufacturing defects.
motivation: Row Hammer poses a critical security threat causing system-wide crashes through uncorrectable DRAM errors, requiring efficient mitigation without prohibitive performance costs.
method: The system identifies which DRAM addresses are vulnerable to Row Hammer attacks through 3-week experiments on real DRAM modules. Starting at boot, it periodically accesses these vulnerable addresses to prevent the bit flips that cause uncorrectable errors. Instead of using the main CPU for this task, it offloads the periodic accesses to a separate processor (a CXL SmartNIC—a specialized chip with its own CPU, connected via CXL, a high-speed connection standard).
key_novelty: The core innovation is handling Row Hammer defense on a separate CXL SmartNIC instead of the main CPU, eliminating performance overhead.
contributions: Characterization of Row Hammer-induced uncorrectable errors showing they manifest only at specific manufacturing-defect-prone DRAM addresses
H-TAROT: Software-based RH defense using periodic access to vulnerable addresses with low implementation complexity
S-TAROT: SmartNIC-based offloading of RH mitigation via CXL interconnect reducing host performance penalty
Experimental validation showing S-TAROT achieves 0.1-1.0% overhead versus 1.5-28.2% for H-TAROT across SPECrate 2017 and Redis workloads

metrics.other: H-TAROT overhead: 1.5% execution time (SPECrate 2017), 28.2% tail latency (Redis); S-TAROT overhead: 0.1% execution time, 1.0% tail latency

limitations: Limitations of the approach not discussed in abstract; evaluation focused on SmartNIC-connected systems.
